questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the language, and the fact that I have visited Lisbon before, thereby feeling a bit familiar.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was such a stressfull process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration opened at 10 in the morning, and it was first come, first served. I did not get any of the courses I applied for back home, as all of them were taken. It was difficult to figure out which courses were in English, and it was your own responsibility to make sure that you did not choose courses that overlapped, which was very hard, as the amount of English courses were limited. if you did not get enough courses, or the courses that you wanted, you had to print out a blanket. Then you could attend the classes and ask the professors if the would allow you to attend their class. Some professors were understanding, others got super annoyed. Everyone I have talked to was very stressed out and uncomfortable, as no onegot their courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get any of the classes I applied for, but I was lucky that I only had to ask one professor if I could attend his class. He was very nice and let me in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To prepare yourself that you will not get any of your classes, and that you have to ask professors to attend their classes. Therefore, do not stress about the registration, it will be fixed later on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not high, it was quite easy. But the exams were hard. Compared to the teaching, the exams were way too hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were specific attendance requirements, you were evaluated based on your participation, and you had way more courses and thereby longer and more days at school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Philosophy of Art, The Study of Cultures, Classical Culture, Language and Communication, The Study of Human Language.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Philosophy of Art. The teacher was very dedicated and the teaching was interesting.

questions.answer: Santa Clara Market, Cascais, Sintra, Porto, Madeira, Surfing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone was super nice and sweet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That we are very privileged in Denmark, as we get payed to go to University and have a very high salary.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and laid back approach.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is a very different way to go to University, but also very interesting to experience. Every exam is written in hand and no notes are allowed. You have to remember everything yourself. Also, all exams are in the same week. The last week of my exchange I had 2 exams on Tuesday and 3 exams on thursday.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend the classes. Or else the exams will be difficult.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet all amazing people from around the world and get to know their cultures. Especially the Portuguese culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Applying for courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No. I really recommend Lisbon.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
